implementation_anchors.observed_contract: DEFAULT_GRID is the nine complementary splits (.005,.045) through (.045,.005); freeze_allocation minimizes the maximum remaining log threshold, equivalent to maximizing min(alpha_i E1,beta_i E2), then freezes the selected split before fresh confirmation.
alpha is construction-time threshold/reporting configuration; the underlying log_e(mu0) path is delegated to the same V3 stream and is alpha-independent.
The persisted validator tests pilot freeze, fresh post-pilot reporting, replay/tamper behavior and fixed/nine-pair stopping baselines; it is not itself a same-history off-target CI theorem.

independent_derivation.selector_equivalence: Minimizing max(log(1/(alpha_i E1)),log(1/(beta_i E2))) is equivalent to maximizing min(i E1,(10-i)E2).
independent_derivation.selection_region: For selected i and r=E1/E2, adjacent-grid optimality yields (9-i)/i <= r <= (10-i)/(i-1), with the natural 0/infinity boundary conventions for i=9/i=1.
independent_derivation.crossing_to_sum_bound: If alpha_i E1>=1, use the largest allowed r to minimize E1+E2; if beta_i E2>=1, use the smallest allowed r. Both cases give E1+E2 >= 90/(delta*i*(10-i)). Since max_i i(10-i)=25, selected crossing implies E1+E2>=3.6/delta.
independent_derivation.anytime_bound: If E1 and E2 are valid e-processes under the same joint target null and filtration, (E1+E2)/2 is an e-process by conditional-expectation linearity; no channel independence is required. Ville therefore gives P(any selected target-null crossing)<=1/(1.8/delta)=5 delta/9. At delta=.05 this is 1/36=0.027777777777777776.
independent_derivation.tie_scope: The persisted selector's deterministic tie-breaking does not invalidate the inclusive selection-region argument; boundary ties satisfy the same inequalities.

material_scope_corrections: The 5 delta/9 result is a fixed-target-null decision/selected-crossing theorem for the exact nine-split minimax geometry, conditional on each channel process being e-valid under the joint target null. It is not a theorem for arbitrary alpha selectors.
No independence between the two channel e-processes is needed for the average-e-process step; common-filtration e-validity under the joint null is the relevant requirement.

The theorem does not imply simultaneous numerical confidence coverage at an unknown theta != mu0, because the selector uses E(mu0) while true-parameter coverage depends on E(theta); no deterministic relation is established in the audited artifacts.

The fresh-confirm wrapper is a separate stronger portable mechanism for post-selection numerical reporting: it freezes selection on the pilot and starts fresh reporting streams after the frozen prefix. The same-history target-null theorem should not be described as the basis of fresh-confirm validity.
The stored 500k Monte Carlo point estimate has incomplete replay provenance because seed/algorithm are absent; this affects exact historical replay only, not the algebraic theorem.
